plain_description.what: Checks 58 stored judge-verdict caches (about 158,000 rows) for whether they record why a judge answer ended: finished normally, cut off by the length limit, or blocked by a content filter. It also fixes the shared judge-call code to keep provider IDs and store refusals. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: A cut-off judge answer can look like a wrong verdict. The thesis needs to know whether its stored results can tell the two apart.
plain_description.information: This shows which results can be checked for truncation, and it prevents silent data loss in future runs. Result: only 7 of 58 caches record the finish reason. All main boards are among the 51 that cannot tell a cut-off from a wrong answer, apart from crude proxies. Future calls now record provider IDs and store refusals as unusable rows. The per-model length probe was not run.
